Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the shared street rendered with owner-coloured slots, shared-market phase alternation, and SFX/animations (per AGENTS.md §8), so competitive ownership is visually and audibly unambiguous.

## Context

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. This planning-created child (per AC5 “deferred to a planning child” and producer Q2 “planning”) captures the deferred rendering scope for the next milestone. Worker must use core-engine animation helpers with `soundManager` + `sfx` (AGENTS.md §8: every animated action needs sound + animation; SFX keys via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, no literals).

## Scope

- Competitive scene (Phaser scene) with SLL layout.
- Owner-coloured street: each placed business's street slot tinted by owner (e.g. player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is immediately readable.
- Shared-market phase alternation: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day with visible whose-turn affordance.
- SFX/animations for all competitive actions (deal/flip/place/discard/illegal) via helpers + `SoundManager`, respecting reduced-motion and mute.
- Turn alternation SFX/animation sequencing so AI actions are visible (delayed AI turn like Coloretto precedent).

## Out of scope

- Engine state/phase/income/AI/Monte Carlo (parent epic siblings).
- Game-selector entry — include only when the scene is ready for play (within this child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Competitive scene renders the shared street with per-slot owner colour (player vs AI unambiguously distinct); SLL layout used (no hardcoded pixel positions).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared-market phase alternation is visible (whose turn) and input is gated to the active player; AI turn is animated with a brief delay.
- [ ] **AC3:** Every competitive action that uses a core-engine animation helper is wired with SFX (via helper `soundManager`/`sfx` params or `GameEventEmitter`/`SoundManager`); SFX keys follow `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention; reduced-motion and mute respected.
- [ ] **AC4:** Build + unit tests pass; smoke browser coverage for the scene.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScene.ts` — Competitive scene (owner-coloured street, phase alternation, SFX).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveRenderer.ts` — Owner-colour helpers (tinting by ownerId).
- `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` source of truth for SFX keys.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene.browser.test.ts` — Smoke/browser coverage.

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode (engine-only; rendering deferred here per AC5)
- Siblings: state, phase, income/events, AI strategy, Monte Carlo (engine foundation this child renders)
- AGENTS.md §8 — Every action with animation must have SFX

# Feature: Hybrid Look-Ahead and Difficulty Scaling

## Summary
Extend scoreBankOption to hybrid visible + pipeline look-ahead (top-N market/deck cards) with look-ahead depth/aggressiveness scaled by difficulty (Easy < Medium < Hard) via aiPlanningHorizon() horizon factor.

## Target Outcome
BankingGreedyStrategy considers both visible unaffordable targets and anticipated near-future targets; Easy hoards less/deeper look-ahead than Hard.

## Definition of Done
- Heuristic considers (a) visible unaffordable targets (hand + market row) and (b) anticipated near-future targets via look-ahead into the market/deck pipeline (top-K deck or market pipeline inspection; bounded to depth).
- Look-ahead depth reduced at lower difficulties (proposed defaults: Easy 0–1, Medium 2–3, Hard 4 — documented in comments; adjust if state.market.deck shape differs).
- Factors: bankedActions, targetCost vs coins (closeness = 1 - gap/cost), aiPlanningHorizon() horizon/cap, bankHeadroom = (2-banked)/2; tuning thresholds documented (closeness < 0.05 -> 0, raw < 1 -> 0).
- Easy hoards strictly less than Hard on shared state (F1 difficulty test passes); no over-hoard at cap; pipeline empty/unavailable falls back to visible-only without crash.
- npm run build + unit tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Hybrid heuristic (visible + pipeline look-ahead) implemented with difficulty-gated depth.
2. Difficulty scaling: Easy look-ahead/aggressiveness < Hard (same state, different decision documented and tested).
3. All factors (banked, closeness, horizon/cap, headroom) applied; tuning documented in comments.
4. Fallback: empty pipeline does not throw; visible-only valuation still works.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add helper getLookAheadTargets(state, depth): reads state.market.deck / pipeline or equivalent (inspect MainStreetState first); bounded to depth; returns Business/Upgrade/Event cards with value estimate.
- Make scoreBankOption(state, difficulty?) accept optional DifficultyName (defaults to state.config.difficultyName or Medium); map difficulty -> {depth, aggressivenessMultiplier}.
- BankingGreedyStrategy passes difficulty through to scoreBankOption; apply multiplier to final bank score.
- Wire tests to pass difficulty explicitly for deterministic coverage.

## Dependencies
- F2: Additive BankingGreedyStrategy core (needs BankingGreedyStrategy + scoreBankOption gate to extend).

## Deliverables
- Updated scoreBankOption + getLookAheadTargets helpers in MainStreetAiStrategy.ts with difficulty scaling
- Inline comments explaining depth map and tuning thresholds
- F1 difficulty test passing at hard vs easy extremes

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` (read pipeline shape)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` (market/deck pipeline)
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`

## Constraints
- Keep look-ahead narrow (few cards, top of deck/pipeline); if pipeline shape is unavailable or look-ahead proves noisy, narrow to visible with documented fallback and OPEN QUESTION.
- Main Street only.
data.title: Hybrid look-ahead and difficulty scaling

# Walk-on applicant gating

## Summary
Gate staff walk-on applicant generation on whether the player owns a deployed business of a matching type (based on allowedBusinessTypes).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Type gating**: A specialist staff applicant only walks on when the player has at least one deployed business whose name or synergy type matches the applicant's allowedBusinessTypes.
2. **No false positives**: If the player owns no matching business type, specialist applicants do not appear (the applicant roll is still consumed but a generalist may appear instead).
3. **Generalist fallback**: Generalist staff (with broad type coverage) can still appear when no specialist match exists, preserving walk-on flow.
4. **Existing behavior preserved**: The applicant chance formula (min(income + rep, 15)%) remains unchanged; only the card selection is filtered.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `resolveStaffApplicant()`, filter the staff deck to only cards whose allowedBusinessTypes match at least one deployed business
- If the filtered deck is empty, fall back to generalist cards (those with broad type coverage)
- If no cards match at all, skip the applicant entirely
- Update the help text in the applicant overlay to explain the gating

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` -- updated resolveStaffApplicant()
- Unit tests: walk-on eligibility gating, generalist fallback, no-applicant scenarios

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts`
- `tests/main-street/walk-on-applicant-gating.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: CG-0MU3BNO590066H75 -- Staff business-type matching engine

# Staff underlay rendering and tooltips

## Summary
Render a graphical staff-count underlay (count badge) on business slots that display employed staff, plus a tooltip that enumerates each employed staff member and their effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff count badge**: A small graphical overlay on each business slot showing the number of employed staff (e.g. a rounded badge in the corner of the slot, or a subtle count underlay beneath the card).
2. **Tooltip enumeration**: Hovering a business slot with employed staff shows a tooltip that lists each employed staff member's name, their allowedBusinessTypes, and their active effects (income bonus, reputation bonus, special abilities).
3. **Tooltips aggregated**: Tooltip aggregates the business's own info (income, reputation, synergy) with the employed staff's buffs.
4. **No overlay conflicts**: The staff underlay does not break existing upgrade overlays (level badge, income display), synergy animations, or sold-state visuals (SOLD overlay).
5. **Empty state**: Slots with no employed staff show no badge and tooltip shows only business info.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `drawBusinessSlot()` in MainStreetRenderer.ts, after applying upgrade overlays, add a count badge rectangle/text if business.employedStaff.length > 0
- Badge positioned at bottom-right corner of slot (SLL-defined anchor)
- Extend tooltip zone to show staff enumeration when employed staff exist
- Reuse existing tooltip rendering infrastructure (buildCardTooltipInfo or similar) with staff enumeration data

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` -- staff count badge + tooltip enumeration
- Browser test: staff underlay + tooltip rendering
- Visual confirmation: badge visible at all zoom levels, tooltip readable

## Key Files

# Staff effect scoping integration

## Summary
Wire staff buff effects to apply only to their employed business slot, not street-wide. Street-wide staff skills (cost cutter, brand ambassador, negotiator, ops salary) continue to aggregate as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-business income buff**: Staff income bonuses apply only to the business they are employed at (via employedAtSlot or business.employedStaff). Not visible on other businesses or street-wide.
2. **Per-business reputation buff**: Staff reputation bonuses apply only to their employed business.
3. **Street-wide skills preserved**: Staff with street-wide effects (Cost Cutter, Brand Ambassador, Negotiator, Operations Manager salary) continue to aggregate across the street.
4. **No double-counting**: Staff effects are not applied both per-business AND street-wide.
5. **Backward compatibility**: Existing staff without allowedBusinessTypes (generalists with hand-slot focus) continue to work as before with no per-business effects.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `MainStreetAdjacency.ts`, when computing per-business income, read buff data from `business.employedStaff` instead of filtering `state.staffCards` by employedAtSlot
- Street-wide skill aggregation (in `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` and related functions) continues to filter by employedAtSlot (which remains set on the StaffCard for tracking)
- Update `computeStaffSalaryCost()` to account for new state model
- Verify existing test suite (staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts) passes with new state model

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` -- per-business buff reads from employedStaff
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` -- street-wide aggregation unchanged
- Unit tests: per-business buff scoping, street-wide skill preservation, no double-counting
- Existing tests pass: staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts, staff-skill-buffs.test.ts

## Goal

Write integration tests for undo/redo with challenge completions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Test: undo-cancel — player undoes an action that completed a challenge but cancels the undo via dialog; the challenge remains completed and score bonus intact.
2. Test: undo-confirm — player undoes an action that completed a challenge and confirms; the challenge completion is revoked (removed from challengesCompleted, completed flag cleared, activity log entry removed, score bonus reverted).
3. Test: redo after undo-confirm — redo re-applies the action and re-completes the challenge; no duplicate log entries or celebrations.
4. Test: redo after undo-cancel — redo is available (state unchanged) and re-applies the action with the same completion.
5. Test: no double-celebration — completing a challenge mid-turn and then ending the turn does not fire the end-of-turn celebration again.
6. Tests cover at least 2 different challenge types (one resource, one placement).
